chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haitham al-Ajali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlul narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) looked at Ali, Hasan, and Husayn (peace be upon them) and wept, and said: 'You are the weak ones after me.'
Al-Mufaddal said: So I said to him: 'What is the meaning of that, O son of the Messenger of Allah?'
He said: 'Its meaning is that you are the Imams after me,'
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says: 'And We want to bestow favor upon those who were considered weak on earth and make them Imams and make them the inheritors.'
This verse is applicable to us until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفُونَ: the weak ones (those who were given favor)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's tears when looking at Ali, Hasan, and Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the Prophet’s tears stemmed from foreseeing the future oppression of the Ahl al-Bayt, redefining 'al-mustad'afun' (the weak) not as the powerless, but as the divinely appointed Imams and inheritors. This interpretation establishes a continuous theological link between the verse in Surah Al-Qasas and the Imamate, affirming that this status remains valid for the Twelve Imams until the Day of Judgment.
